text:
Anaheim played the better game and still lost it. The Ducks led 2-0 after a first period that ended in 21 seconds of chaos, Tim Washe scoring on a 1 percent chance at 19:22 and Beckett Sennecke tipping one in at 19:43. ANA out-chanced BOS 1.44 to 0.70 in expected goals in that period, and finished with 71 shot attempts to 45 and a 55 percent share of simulated replays.

Boston won it on the power play. Frederic Brunet snapped one home with the man advantage in the second, David Pastrnak tied it on a backhand early in the third, and Elias Lindholm tipped in the go-ahead goal at 8:18 on a 58 percent chance. BOS went 3 for 4 with the extra man while ANA went 0 for 5, and both sides generated almost identical power-play expected goals (0.98 to 0.99). At even strength, BOS actually led 2.65 to 2.43 in expected goals, so the special teams gap was about finishing, not volume. Matthew Poitras added an even-strength backhand at 16:20 to seal it.

The goaltending was the other swing. Michael DiPietro stopped 26 of 28 and saved 1.94 goals more than the shots deserved, while Lukas Dostal allowed four on 22 shots, a goals-saved-above-expected mark of -0.37. Pastrnak finished with a goal and an assist, and James Hagens collected two assists in just over 10 minutes.
